author: nc1234
content:
So I was working on getting Lodestar to pass the fork choice compliance tests and
noticed several vectors where the same block arrives multiple times at different
times. Lodestar calls `on_block()` once and ignores the re-deliveries, but the
comp test generation calls it each time, which wipes the PTC votes in the store. That
moves the expected head, so Lodestar fails those vectors on a head mismatch.
[#5495](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5495) is my fix for that.

But I'd like some clarification in general: is it possible for `on_block()` to be
called more than once with the same block?

The only place I can find that specifies invocation is phase0/fork-choice.md 
"`on_block(store, block)` whenever a block `block: SignedBeaconBlock` is received"
 which doesn't say anything about the block being new. And while gossip validation
does ignore already-seen blocks, that check reads `seen.proposer_slots`, which is
only written inside `validate_beacon_block_gossip`. So a block that arrived via
`BeaconBlocksByRange`/`ByRoot` was never recorded there, and a later gossip copy of
it passes the first-block check.

I dug through some historical discussion, specifically
[#1891](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/1891#issuecomment-644332501):

> Specifically in this case, since on_block(b) is an idempotent operation, an
> optimized client can choose to not re-run on_block(b). Note that this still
> maintains the exact same behavior (w.r.t. the state and store) as the
> specification!

which is what Lodestar relies on. Is that still the
intent? cc. <@592004585506340885> <@755590043632140352>
